headline: Highest risk is medium: aci can ingest shared content and egress broadly while dbt-core can act on warehouse data, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways in default integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci supports direct function calls or MCP and broad network egress, so it can ingest external content and pass it into tool workflows. dbt-core is a data-engineering agent that can consume warehouse inputs, but no explicit provenance or isolation is documented. The pairwise bridge is plausible in default integrations, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF aci receives attacker-controlled content through MCP or API inputs
IF dbt-core consumes aci-produced text or files as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP or file bridge between the agents
Require explicit allowlists for inputs passed from aci to dbt-core
Add a human review step before dbt-core executes generated instructions
Strip instruction-like text from aci outputs before forwarding
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and parser hardening

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad egress, while dbt-core touches warehouse data and can call a warehouse. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data can flow from aci into dbt-core outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF aci and dbt-core share files, environment variables, or credentials
IF warehouse queries or generated artifacts include CRM/email/support fields from aci
mitigations: Separate credentials for each agent
Keep distinct workspaces and temp directories
Redact sensitive fields before passing data to dbt-core
Review outbound network destinations for aci
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention and workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and direct function calls/MCP, while dbt-core is runnable but has no elevated privileges or write surfaces documented here. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so a hard conflict is not established. Uncertainty stays low because the write path is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same warehouse objects or shared files
IF an orchestrator gives them concurrent mutable access without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output schemas or directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Use locks for shared mutable resources
Review dbt run targets before execution
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and dbt-core can act on warehouse data, so aci output could become dbt-core input in a default automation chain. No verification or provenance controls are documented, making cascading mistakes plausible. Because dbt-core is not shown to autonomously send external actions, this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF dbt-core treats aci-generated SQL, metrics, or narratives as authoritative
IF downstream jobs execute without a review or validation step
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema and SQL linting before execution
Have dbt-core compare outputs against source data checks
Limit aci to draft-only recommendations
requires-engineering: add signed handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, support, and calendar data, which can include regulated personal data, while dbt-core processes warehouse data. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out. Because the data classes are sensitive and the deployment details are unknown, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data from aci is loaded into dbt-core-managed warehouse workflows
IF the warehouse or downstream services have stricter residency or retention rules than aci
mitigations: Classify data before sharing between agents
Keep regulated data out of dbt-core runs
Document retention and deletion rules for both systems
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement
